events.title: Chlothar II issues the Edict of Paris
events.description: After reuniting the Frankish kingdoms, the Merovingian king Chlothar II issued the Edict of Paris following a church council. Its 24 articles confirmed the rights of the church and aristocracy and required royal officials to be appointed from the regions they governed.
events.html: After reuniting the Frankish kingdoms, the Merovingian king Chlothar II issued the Edict of Paris following a church council. Its 24 articles confirmed the rights of the church and aristocracy and required royal officials to be appointed from the regions they governed.

events.title: Dagobert I becomes ruler of all the Frankish kingdoms
events.description: Dagobert I, king of Austrasia since 623, became ruler of Neustria and Burgundy as well, and so of all the Frankish kingdoms. After him, real power passed increasingly to the mayors of the palace.
events.html: Dagobert I, king of Austrasia since 623, became ruler of Neustria and Burgundy as well, and so of all the Frankish kingdoms. After him, real power passed increasingly to the mayors of the palace.

events.title: Caliph al-Hakim has the Holy Sepulchre demolished
events.description: On the orders of the Fatimid caliph al-Hakim, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem was torn down. Its destruction shocked Christendom and was remembered as a grievance when the First Crusade was preached.
events.html: On the orders of the Fatimid caliph al-Hakim, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem was torn down. Its destruction shocked Christendom and was remembered as a grievance when the First Crusade was preached.

events.title: Cnut's Danes defeat Edmund Ironside at the Battle of Assandun
events.description: A Danish army led by King Cnut defeated the English under King Edmund Ironside at Assandun, in Essex. A treaty then divided England between them, and when Edmund died shortly afterwards Cnut became undisputed king, as agreed.
events.html: A Danish army led by King Cnut defeated the English under King Edmund Ironside at Assandun, in Essex. A treaty then divided England between them, and when Edmund died shortly afterwards Cnut became undisputed king, as agreed.

events.title: Robert Guiscard's Normans defeat Alexios I at Dyrrhachium
events.description: In the Byzantine–Norman wars, the Normans of southern Italy under Robert Guiscard, Duke of Apulia and Calabria, defeated the army of Emperor Alexios I Komnenos outside Dyrrhachium, the major Byzantine stronghold in the western Balkans.
events.html: In the Byzantine–Norman wars, the Normans of southern Italy under Robert Guiscard, Duke of Apulia and Calabria, defeated the army of Emperor Alexios I Komnenos outside Dyrrhachium, the major Byzantine stronghold in the western Balkans.

events.title: Louis XIV revokes the Edict of Nantes
events.description: By the Edict of Fontainebleau, Louis XIV outlawed Protestant worship in France. Some 200,000 Huguenots fled abroad to England, the Dutch Republic and Prussia, taking valuable skills with them.
events.html: By the Edict of Fontainebleau, Louis XIV outlawed Protestant worship in France. Some 200,000 Huguenots fled abroad to England, the Dutch Republic and Prussia, taking valuable skills with them.

events.title: Mason and Dixon complete their boundary survey
events.description: Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon finished surveying the boundary between Pennsylvania and Maryland. Their line later became the symbolic divide between free and slave states.
events.html: Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon finished surveying the boundary between Pennsylvania and Maryland. Their line later became the symbolic divide between free and slave states.

events.title: The United States takes possession of Alaska
events.description: At Sitka, the Russian flag was lowered and the US flag raised, formally transferring Alaska, bought for 7.2 million dollars. Critics mocked the deal as 'Seward's Folly' until gold and oil proved its value.
events.html: At Sitka, the Russian flag was lowered and the US flag raised, formally transferring Alaska, bought for 7.2 million dollars. Critics mocked the deal as 'Seward's Folly' until gold and oil proved its value.

events.title: The British Broadcasting Company is founded
events.description: Wireless manufacturers formed the British Broadcasting Company to run Britain's first national radio service. Under John Reith it became the public British Broadcasting Corporation in 1927.
events.html: Wireless manufacturers formed the British Broadcasting Company to run Britain's first national radio service. Under John Reith it became the public British Broadcasting Corporation in 1927.

intl.name: World Menopause Day
intl.description: Designated by the International Menopause Society and supported by the World Health Organisation, World Menopause Day raises awareness of the menopause and the support options available for improving health and wellbeing for the over one billion women worldwide who will reach this stage of life by 2025.
